content:
anya: hi all, day 1. trying to build runtime from source on an Ubuntu 18 VM and I get a bunch of linker errors like: 

/usr/bin/ld: /usr/lib/gcc/x86_64-linux-gnu/7/../../../../lib64/libstdc++.so: undefined reference to `__cxa_demangle'
/usr/bin/ld: warning: libstdc++.so.6, needed by ./libfoo.so, may conflict with libstdc++.so.6
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status

anya: `g++ --version` shows 7.5.0. It looks like an ABI mismatch?

jordi: welcome @anya! yep that's an ABI/libstdc++ version issue. our builds expect GCC 11+ (libstdc++ ABI changes). two quick fixes: 1) install g++-11 and export CXX=g++-11 before cmake, or 2) use the dev container `redwood/dev-runtime:toolchain-ubuntu20` which has the right toolchain.

anya: thanks. tried `sudo apt install g++-11` then `update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/g++ g++ /usr/bin/g++-11 100` and re-ran cmake — build progressed further.

jordi: nice. also watch out for mixed prebuilt third_party libs that were compiled against a newer libstdc++; if you see versioned symbol errors like GLIBCXX_3.4.30 not found, you might need to rebuild those deps or pin the container.

runtime-ci-bot: note: CI runs on ubuntu-20 toolchain image. If you open a PR, include `//ci:use-toolchain=ubuntu20` to match CI.

anya: opening a small docs PR to add a short section "Recommended local toolchain" with commands to install g++-11 and a note about using our dev image. tagging @jordi and @emma for review. thanks!

emma: perfect. also ping infra if you want us to spin up a temporary ubuntu20 dev host. glhf :)
